steps.player: Tell me more about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.

steps.player: Phew!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Hey! Who's telling this story?

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Can I finish the story without interruptions?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Carry on dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: And so the blood feud continued.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: The smoke damage was atrocious, I had to replace my entire wardrobe.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, dear.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.

steps.speaker: Mord Gunnars
steps.text: But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Oh, hello stranger. If you're new to town you should speak with our ruler, King Gjuki Sorvott IV. He'll want to meet you - he always wants to have a chat with any strangers in town. They could be spies you know.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Yes, spies from Neitiznot. They're everywhere. Apparently. That's what the King says anyway.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: So what do you do here?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Me? I'm a cook. Fish dishes a speciality. I hate fish. But fish is about all we have. Except for yak. But we're not allowed to eat yak.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Why not, is yak meat bad for you?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Certainly not! Yak meat is both sweet and delicately flavoured. Yak is juicier than buffalo and elk - but never gamey. It goes wonderfully well with a glass of red wine, and it's healthy too!

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: So why aren't you allowed to eat it?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: King's orders. They breed and eat yaks on Neitiznot, so WE'RE not allowed to. It's unjust I tell you! I had a dream last night about a juicy fillet of yak, served on a bed of deep-fried seaweed and topped with a garnish

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: That's a little sad. So do you have any cooked food I could buy?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: No. It would only be fish anyway. Why would you want to eat fish?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Well, I wouldn't mind a few shark and swordfish steaks as back-up you know.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Keepa Kettilon
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: If you insist. Sorry the stock is so low, but I just can't be bothered to cook any more.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Hello. What's happening in town at the moment?

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: These dwarves have arrived from Keldagrim - the Chancellor has asked me to look after them, but they are eating all of our food and drinking all of our booze.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: They are organising some sort of trade agreement. I don't know what they are trading.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Brendt

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Bored, bored, bored. These Fremenniks are taking ages.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.player: Hey, they're doing their best. You arrived early.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Hey, we arrived precisely when we told your representatives. Lack of planning on your part does not constitute an emergency on my part.

starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-first-meetings-in-jatizso-t.text: Please, someone get these guys their ore quickly. They are eating all the good food on the island, and complaining about it!

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Thank you [Fremennik name]. If only our miners were as efficient as you.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Right. Now let us get down to business, young [Fremennik name]. Let us hope we have no more interruptions.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Neitiznot's Burgher, Mawnis Burowgar, is a simpleton and a fool.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I have bested him before and will do so again!

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: He is surely plotting a new plan to defeat me.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: He's up to something, he's always up to something.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I will not be kept in the dark about his plans any longer. I must know what underhand tricks he'll use to undermine me. He's out to get me! Get me I say!

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Ahem, I see, sir. How may I help in this matter?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Well, I have heard that some call you 'bard' in Rellekka. Your lyre-playing reputation has carried this far.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: You want me to play the lyre? Well actually, I've been working on a few tunes in my spare time. I have this new song about-

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Silence! I do not wish to hear your wailing. All bards are charlatans and fools.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: However, a fool is exactly what I need right now.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: It's a great tune, very catching, you'll love-

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Bah! Bards are all the same, they never shut up! If I need to be entertained I'll hire a mime; maybe I'll get some rest then. Now if you'll listen, I'll explain what I need you to do.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: In the past I have sent my Spymaster to 'entertain' the Burgher, and to see what he can find out.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: You see, the Burgher of Neitiznot and his aides like a drink when they are being entertained, and their tongues are loose when they drink.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: However, yesterday my spy had an accident and could no longer help me in this task. However he is still stationed on Neitiznot.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So this is a covert operation into Neitiznot? You need me to infiltrate the Burgher's hall, undercover, and uncover his evil plans?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Exactly, [Fremennik name]. So are you interested?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Sounds like a task for an elite adventurer like myself. Mission accepted.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Excellent, [Fremennik name], you and I will get on very well.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So what is the easiest way to get to Neitiznot?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: I suggest you catch Mord's ferry back to Rellekka and then catch a ferry from there.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: Are you sure that's the best way?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: You may find a way across the islands, but the bridges are almost certainly broken, and there are trolls which are a bit of a nuisance. The ferry is probably both quicker and safer.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Oh, there is one more thing. In order to gain an audience with the Burgher, you will need my Spymaster's, err, costume.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: The costume is in my chest. Don't forget to pick up all the pieces.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Then travel to Neitiznot and talk to my Spymaster. He is still over there. He will fill you in with the details, and you may report to him.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Oh, the Spymaster is a secretive kind of guy. He will require a password. The password is 'free stuff please'.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: What sort of password is that?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Don't ask me, it was his idea.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: His name is Slug Hemligssen, but don't expect him to answer to it.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.player: So how will I recognise him?

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.speaker: King Sorvott IV
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-kin.text: Don't worry, you'll find him.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Brendt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: Well it seemed rude not to finish the food they gave us.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: Feel free to leave it. Please leave.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-bre.text: I'll just finish the roast off.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.speaker: Grundt
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.text: Ah, yes. Now that's what I call a meal.

starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.speaker: Vanligga Gastfrihet
starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to-gru.text: That's funny, I called it fourteen meals yesterday.

jestering-around-before-departing-from-j.text: Well, what are you waiting for? Hop to it!

options.text: Tell me about Neitiznot's geography.

steps.player: Tell me about Neitiznot's geography.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Sure.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, as I have mentioned, I am from an island called Jatizso, while my wife is from another island called Neitiznot. Neitiznot is a far less sophisticated and successful island which will not see reason with Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ne it iz not!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ja it iz so!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ahem, anyway, the islands are in a small volcanic archipelago north of here.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Along with the main isles there are numerous small islands and a frozen northern island that was recently overrun by trolls.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Jatizso is rich in minerals, and trades extensively, while Neitiznot has stolen all the decent arable land.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Well, that wealth is needed to buy the food from Neitiznot at extortionate rates!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Only because Jatizso hogs all the wealth!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Ok Maria, stop that!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Ok dear!

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Where was I? Yup, that covers the layout of the islands.

options.text: Tell me about the islands' history.

steps.text: (Same as Mord Gunnars' "Tell me more about Jatizso's history" option)

options.text: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.player: Tell me about Burger Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Well Burgher Mawnis Burowgar is a gentle soul at heart. His kinsfolk are happy and content with their lot.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: 'Soft' is the word we use in Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Well a soft Burgher is better than a stupid King.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, there was a time when Burgher Burowgar was similar to King Sorvott.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Argumentative, short tempered; I am sure you know what I mean.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: The change happened when the trolls came and razed Neitiznot to the ground.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: You mean while Neitiznot's militias were assaulting Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Yes, well our tribes have been at war for nearly four generations now.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Anyway, the Burgher lost his wife and youngest son in the trolls' raid and has been a changed man since.

steps.speaker: Mord
steps.text: May their journey to our ancestors' halls be swift.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Personally, I am much happier with the considerate Burgher we have now.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Neitiznot?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Let's set sail then.
Leaving Rellekka for Neitiznot.

options.text: I just stopped to say 'hello'.

jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.speaker: Maria Gunnars
jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.text: Hi, [Fremennik name], you should speak with Burgher Mawnis Burowgar in the main chambers. Do you have any questions?

jestering-around-learning-about-neitizno.prompt: What do you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about your husband.

steps.player: Tell me about your husband.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: My husband is a typical Fremennik, being both headstrong and brave.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: We fell in love when we were young, but as there was a war between our isles, we were ordered to stop seeing each other by our parents.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: This didn't stop Mord climbing the wailing tower, on his side of the channel between our isles, to sing to me every night.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: After Mord's voice broke, his singing voice was lost, but I still listened to his terrible sonnets each and every night.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Until one night there was no singing! Then, far below me, I heard a gentle voice calling my name.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Mord had stolen his father's boat to come and fetch me from my prison

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: and from that day forth we have lived in Rellekka.

options.text: Tell me about Jatizso.

steps.player: Tell me about Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: My husband does not speak of the inhabitants of the isle of Jatizso much.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: He has little positive to say about his parents, so he chooses not to speak of them in my presence. The only thing I've noticed is that everyone on that island seems very sad...

steps.prompt: Who do you want to know about?

options.text: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.player: Tell me about King Sorvott IV.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: King Sorvott IV follows in the footsteps of a line of kings who have reigned since Jatizso himself passed away. It is rumoured that the King has no heir and is seeking a bride to bear him children. Given his

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: personality I'm not surprised he hasn't found a bride yet!

options.text: What were you saying before?
Tell me about Neitiznot.

steps.player: Tell me about Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: To be honest with you, I do not keep up to date with all the goings on here now that I have a home in Rellekka.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: However, Neitiznot seems a happy place! The Burgher seems a wiser rule than King Sorvott, although I believe he is worried about the trolls at the moment. They seem to be a big threat.

options.text: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.player: Can you ferry me to Rellekka?

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Sure.
Leaving Neitiznot for Rellekka.

options.text: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.player: I have nothing to ask you right now.

steps.speaker: Maria Gunnars
steps.text: Fare thee well.

rope-gathering-rope-delivery.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar

steps.player: I'll do that shortly.

steps.text: Once you have eight pieces of rope and eight split logs I will explain how you can use them to repair the bridges that the trolls attacked a few days ago.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well then, [Fremennik name], are you willing to assist my engineer?

steps.player: I would be happy to help your kinsfolk, Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.text: Ah, a bit more respect. That's better.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.text: Excellent. We are one step closer to putting my plan into action.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.text: Now that the bridges are repaired I feel I can tell you of our plans.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.text: First, I shall have my engineer reward you for you efforts.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.text: [Fremennik name] has repaired both bridges. Please reward [him/her] for [his/her] efforts, Thakkrad.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.player: That is most generous of you, Sir.

bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
bridge-building-talking-to-mawnis-after-.text: We are a generous folk, over here on Neitiznot.

steps.text: Thakkrad Sigmundson hands you 1500 coins.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Good work! Now that you have repaired our bridges I can make the final preparations for our assault on the troll caves.

steps.player: Troll caves!

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Long ago, the ancestors of this isle fought heroically against the troll menace upon these isles.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: But, for the last few generations, we have been preoccupied with fighting our neighbours on Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: In our complacency, the trolls have grown in number and strength and have become increasingly brazen in their raids, attacking our kinsfolk, stealing and destroying our belongings. Now the time has come for

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: us to drive the trolls from this isle. We must defeat their leader, the foul Troll King.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Although I am confident we will be victorious, I am a cautious man.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: We have suffered for many generations and the blood of our ancestors grows weak.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: But now, in this time of prosperity, Fridleif has recruited the bravest Fremennik warriors from far and wide to win back our honour.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Now that you have proven your loyalty, I offer you the honour of leading my forces into battle.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: What say you, [Fremennik name]?

steps.player: I am honoured, Burowgar.
I gratefully accept your offer to lead the charge against your foes.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Excellent! Once Fridleif's militia arrive and are fully equipped we shall head north into the troll caves.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Glory to the Fremenniks.

steps.speaker: Honourguard
steps.text: Death to the trolls.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: I have one last concern. I suspect that King Sorvott may have some idea that we intend to make this raid.

steps.player: I'm afraid that may be true sire.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: If he and his men were willing to aid us in this task then that would not be a problem, however I suspect that Sorvott will see our actions and misinterpret them. He may well attempt to prevent us. I need to know the

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: extent of his knowledge so that I may plan. [Fremennik name], I suspect that you may be able to help us here. I find underhand methods distasteful, however I ask you to go to Jatizso and find the King's plans by whatever means

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: you are familiar with.

steps.player: I can do this sire.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Do you need anything from me to help you?

steps.player: Err, no. I believe I already have all the...contacts I need.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Excellent. Then make your way with haste.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: My militia are still gathering in Rellekka. Have you found out anything about Jatizso's plans yet?

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.player: Not yet sir, but I shall return soon.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Have you found out about Jatizso's plans yet, [Fremennik name]?

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.player: Thanks Thakkrad, i'm on my way there now.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Our militia are still preparing themselves for our raid against the trolls.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Have you found out about Jatizso's plans yet?

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.player: Not yet, but I am on my way there now.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Entering these caves without the support of the Burgher's guards would be suicide.
Entering these caves without support from the Neitiznot militia would be suicide. I should speak with Mawnis Burowgar in Neitiznot.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Hello again, [Fremennik name], I hear you are to be appointed as the Burgher's Champion?

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.player: He said something about leading his forces into battle, but I didn't hear the Burgher use the word 'champion'.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Well you see, Mawnis Burowgar is a superstitious man. He lost a Champion, several years back. It was really embarrassing...

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: The Champion strapped so much armour to himself that he fell straight through the jetty on arrival here and didn't even meet the Burgher.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: So you see, Mawnis won't use the term 'Champion' often, as he believes it brings bad luck.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: If you have any questions I would be happy to answer them.

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: Welcome back [Fremennik name]. How was your time on Neitiznot?

bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.speaker: Maria Gunnars
bridge-building-after-learning-about-maw.text: You should speak with my husband. King Sorvott has been asking for you.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: I hope your mission was successful. Talk with the King, I'm sure he has some things he wishes to discuss with you.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Have you gathered the information about when Neitiznot's bridges will be repaired?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.player: I have, sir. They have been repaired.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Outrageous, how are they working so rapidly?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.player: The Fremennik are a very resourceful folk, your majesty.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: That may be, but we are very different from the vermin on Neitiznot.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: We must amass our troops immediately. We must be ready for Neitiznot's army to attack us.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Chancellor, how are the city's coffers? We will need to pay for weapons and food for our soldiers.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Would you like the financial report now, sir?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Once we have paid for all the supplies you...err...I have ordered, your Royal Highness, then the coffers will be at their lowest ebb for some time. However, if we tighten our belts and delay your plans for extra

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: defences, then-

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: What! That is not acceptable! How am I supposed to run this city when I am surrounded by incompetence!

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Now, more than ever, we need to protect ourselves from the threat from Neitiznot. This is a time of national crisis. Every citizen of Jatizso must bear the burden of protecting our homes. If it means that as

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: citizens we must sacrifice some luxuries for the good of Jatizso, then it must be so. We must raise more taxes.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: But we have already collected Island Taxes this month! We'll never persuade anyone to pay it. Everyone is surviving on coppers as it is.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Yes, well, whatever. Needs must. Think up a new tax.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: A new tax!

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Be quiet serf.
The King ignores your protests.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Yes, I was having a discussion with King Vargas the other day. He was saying some places have taxes for all kinds of things; fur taxes, blueberry taxes, tea taxes, playing card taxes. All we need to do is pick something

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: that lots of people have. How about a Window Tax? We have windows on the island.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: A Window Tax?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Yes, yes. That's an excellent idea. I now institute a new Window Tax. Every building with windows. Other countries have Window Taxes, we need them as well.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.player: Err, what? I'm not sure I agree with-

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: How am I going to sell this one?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Well, you had better find a way, and fast! Oh, [Fremennik name] you seem like someone who gets things done. I now appoint you official tax collector of Jatizso!

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.player: Why would I want to be a tax collector for a-

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Did you say something?

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: Shhh! Please whisper, [Fremennik name]! For both our sakes just agree, otherwise he'll get into one of his moods, and who knows what he'll pronounce.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: [Fremennik name]! I command you to refill the royal coffers! Thorkel will work out the details.
Without free inventory space:

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: You don't have space for the King's tax bag.

return-to-jatizso-becoming-a-tax-collect.text: With free inventory space:

steps.text: You hear Thorkel muttering to himself under his breath.

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: How is this island supposed to develop if we keep spending all our money on his paranoid schemes?

steps.player: Thorkel, can you tell me about this taxation?

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: You need to speak with some of the citizens of Jatizso and collect their taxes.

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: Count the number of windows on each building and tax the people who work inside. 1000 per window.

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: The only people who earn any real money on the island are shopkeepers. Soldiers clearly do not need to be taxed, as paying soldiers' wages is part of the reason for the tax in the first place.

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: Once you have finished collecting the taxes, come and speak to me again.

steps.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
steps.text: Thank you for helping our fine city [Fremennik name].

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.player: Not yet, though I've just noticed that this building has more windows in it than any other building.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Hurry, I need to see my treasury overflowing!

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: King Sorvott IV
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Go and speak with Thorkel if you need to know who to tax.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.player: Can you tell me who I should tax?

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Well, for the Window Tax, only those who use a building.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Go to each of the buildings in town:

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: The armourer's hut and the weaponsmith's hut, the eating hall, and the fish shop; all these buildings need to be taxed. The royal hall doesn't need to be taxed, nor the bank or any empty buildings.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Count the number of windows the building has and then ask one of the people who works there to pay the tax.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: The tax is currently 1000gp per window.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: As you do so your tax bag will fill up slowly. When you've taxed everyone you can, come back here and talk to me or the King.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Oh, hello. Tax collector, huh? You're not going to tax me are you?

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.player: Not right now. You haven't lived here for a while anyway, and the King seems most keen to tax shopkeepers, so I reckon you are tax exempt!

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Mord Gunnars
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Phew! In that case, can I do anything for you?

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.player: Not yet. I have a small task I must complete in order to ingratiate myself with King Sorvott.

return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
return-to-jatizso-after-becoming-a-tax-c.text: Well then, you'd better get on with it.

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: Trogen Konungarde/Kjedelig Uppsen
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: Ah, hello jester. Hey! I've just noticed, you look a little similar to our new champion!

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.player: You have a jester and a fool as a Champion?

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: Trogen Konungarde/Kjedelig Uppsen
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: No, of course not, that would be silly. You just...look similar.

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.player: We must both be outlanders. We all look the same you know.

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: Trogen Konungarde/Kjedelig Uppsen
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: Yes, you're right of course. Anyway, I think the Burgher is in the mood for some more entertainment, so carry on through.

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: Hello jester. Have a chat with the Burgher, I think he's in the mood for jest.

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: I think the Burgher could do with a laugh right now. Why don't you ask him?

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.text: Have you finished your spying task yet?

jestering-again-after-discussing-the-new.player: Not yet. I'll finish it off now.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, good timing. I was just thinking I needed a bit of light entertainment.
The screen fades to black...

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, back again. I hope you've got a new act.

steps.player: Err, of course sire. I assure you this act will be somewhat different.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Get on with it then.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, good timing. I was just thinking I needed a bit of light entertainment.
The screen fades to black...

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: When you said you had a new act you were lying weren't you?

steps.player: I can recite the epic tale of Beowulf if you prefer. It'll only take four or five hours.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: No, no, no, your old act is fine. I've had more than enough Beowulf. My tutor made me study that tale again and again.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Yawwwn**.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Get on with it! The more slapstick, the better.

steps.player: I'm happy to humiliate myself for your entertainment, sire.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: So what do you think of the Burgher's Champion?

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: [He/She] seems honourable and courageous to me.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: What about their collaboration with King Sorvott?

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: Well I trust Mord Gunnars, and he works for the King.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: And the Champion did help repair your bridges.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: Yes, well. So are your militia ready?

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: I have them anchored near Etceteria.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: Then I shall sail the potions to them tonight.

jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
jestering-again-performing-for-the-burgh.text: Then we are ready to launch our raid at dawn?

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.text: Are you ready to make your report, [Fremennik name]?

options.text: Yes, I am.

steps.player: Yes, I am.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Now I will ask you some questions, but be warned I have other sources of information that can corroborate your answers.

steps.player: I am ready to answer your questions.

steps.text: Where are Neitiznot's militia?

options.text: They are in a secluded bay, near Miscellania.
They are in a secluded bay, near Etceteria.

steps.player: They are in a secluded bay, near Etceteria.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: What will Thakkrad deliver to Neitiznot's militia tonight?

options.text: They will be given some potions.

steps.player: They will be given some potions.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Who has been helping Burgher Mawnis Burowgar?

options.text: Chieftain Brundt of Rellekka has been helping Neitiznot.
Advisor Ghrim of Miscellania has been helping Neitiznot.
I have been helping Neitiznot.

steps.text: If any of the incorrect options were picked:

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Do not think you can lie to me. Come back when you are more inclined to give me the information I require.
If all of the correct options were picked:

steps.player: I have been helping Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Hmmm, that is very interesting. I believe you're telling me the truth.

steps.player: I would not lie to you.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Clearly not. Well, here is your fee.
With a full inventory:

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You don't have space for the King's reward.
With free inventory space:
The Spymaster hands you 2500 coins.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Right, [Fremennik name], you had better go and talk to the King. I expect he'll want to discuss your intelligence.

options.text: They will be given some fine ale and meat.
They will be given some party hats and balloons.
They are in a secluded bay, near Rellekka.
No, I need to make a fool of myself again.

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.player: No, I need to make a fool of myself again.

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.text: Please pay more attention to what the Burgher's advisors say this time. Are you ready?
If wearing the jester outfit with nothing equipped in hands:

steps.player: I am ready.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Indeed, you look very dapper in your costume.

steps.player: Hmmm. I'm beginning to think that this spy malarkey is not as cool as I thought.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: You're ready to entertain the Burgher. Good luck with you mission, Operative Budgie. Stay alert.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: When you are done, come back and talk to me to give your report. I will make sure the King is informed.

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.text: If not wearing the jester outfit or with something equipped in hands:

steps.player: I am ready.
I am ready.

steps.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
steps.text: Not dressed like that you're not! You'd better get the rest of your kit, or empty your hands if you have anything in them.

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.speaker: Slug Hemligssen
jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.text: Shhh. Go away. I'm not allowed to talk to you.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: I have just one final task before you leave [Fremennik name].

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: So you admit that it was you who repaired Neitiznot's bridges?

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: I was following your orders, Sir.
I was given strict instructions to go along with Mawnis Burowgar's orders while investigating their island.
As I told your fool of a Spymaster, Neitiznot's militia are not going to attack you.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: Then why does Burgher Mawnis Burowgar amass an army?

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: It is no army Neitiznot has trained, but a raiding party, sire.
Mawnis Burowgar's goal is to see the leader of the trolls beheaded.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: Do you take me for a fool [Fremennik name]? It's all lies!

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: You must have been brainwashed by my cousin! He is EVIL and wants to destroy me! Jah! Tiz so! Jah! Tiz so!

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: Right! That's it! I've had enough!
No more lying! No more biting my tongue! Do I take you for a fool? Yes I do!
You are so paranoid about Neitiznot that you are running this island into the ground!

Neitiznot is not going to attack Jatizso. I'll say it again to try and force it into your thick skull! Neitiznot is not going to attack Jatizso. They don't care about Jatizso. They care about the trolls and Troll King who
are the real threats to the islands. You are so obsessed with your cousin, however, that you stick your head
in the sand whenever it comes to the trolls. But I'm not sure it matters, since I think there is a good chance that you will destroy this village long before the trolls get here!
You do not have to dress in a jester's costume to act the fool, your royal crown is more than enough!

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: No-one has ever talked to me like that before.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: Maybe if they had, you wouldn't be in this mess.
I'd like to see you try.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: So it seems that my cousin's plan is to demonstrate his superiority by killing the Troll King. I cannot let that happen! I will not let him steal the glory.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: You haven't listened to a single word I've been saying, have you?

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: We amass our forces now! There is no time to lose.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: At dawn my men will march upon my ancestor's nemesis, the Troll King.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: Do you even know where to find the Troll King? Your warriors are underfed and tired; your weapons inadequate. You don't stand a chance. Join with your brethren and you may share the glory and perhaps find
a way to make peace between your lands. I'm sure the Burgher would be glad of your aid.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: Bah! Don't be ridiculous! He would just stab me in the back and claim the glory himself. My brave warriors will find the Troll King and slay him first. How could they not, they are Jatizso warriors, not Neitiznot scum.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: You will deliver my decree to Burgher Mawnis Burowgar.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: You shall inform him that my troops attack the western troll caves at dawn and that his interference shall be considered an act of WAR! Long live Jatizso! Long live ME!

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.player: Fine. I give up. I will do this final task for you. After that you're on your own - may the gods be with your troops - they're going to need it.

jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.speaker: King Sorvott IV
jestering-again-reporting-in-returning-t.text: Fine. Take the decree and go.

steps.text: You don't have space for the King's decree
King Sorvott hands you a document.

jestering-again-reporting-in-talking-to-.speaker: King Sorvott IV

If the player has the decree:

steps.player: Not yet.

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: Well, get a move-on.

steps.player: Not yet, I've lost the decree.

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: You've lost it! Bah! It's a good thing I'm used to working with incompetents!
With a full inventory:

steps.player: I'm afraid I don't have the space to carry it.

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: More incompetence! Well, come back when you have.
With open inventory space:
King Sorvott hands you a sealed document.

steps.speaker: King Sorvott IV
steps.text: Well? Get moving!

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: Ah [Fremennik name], the Burgher is keen to see you. Walk on through.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: You should speak to Fridleif or the Burgher about crafting yourself the traditional armour of a Fremennik warrior.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: My militia are en route from Rellekka. Have you found out anything about Jatizso's plans yet?
If the royal decree was lost:

steps.player: I was instructed to give you this, err, now where did I put the King's decree?

steps.text: You should return to King Sorvott to get another copy of his note.

steps.player: I'll be back shortly.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: If the player has the royal decree:

steps.player: I have, sir.
I was instructed to give you this decree by King Sorvott.

steps.text: You hand King Sorvott's document to Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.player: King Sorvott has spies that have learnt of the troops you have trained.
Until recently, they believed that you planned to assault their town.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: The paranoid fool.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: It would bring great shame upon my family to break the truce that was signed between King Sorvott III and my father.

steps.player: Now that Jatizso's spies have learnt of your plans to attack the troll caves, King Sorvott is raising his guards to assault them himself.
I believe he plans to depart before you can be ready.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well, if he thinks the folk of Neitiznot can be intimidated by his threats, he best be ready to accept defeat.

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Blasted spies, how can King Sorvott call himself a Fremennik when he resorts to such dishonourable tactics?

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: We have no time to lose. Fridleif, please guide [Fremennik name] through the traditions laid down by our ancestors.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Once you have completed these rites I shall appoint you as head of my raiding party.

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Indeed, it is written in the sagas of Neitiznot that the Champion of the isle must equip himself with the tools of a Fremennik warrior.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: I offer to act as guide to [Fremennik name] during the traditional rites.

steps.player: Very well. What do these rites entail?

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Firstly, you must equip yourself with the traditional armour of Neitiznot.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: You will need to cull several yaks in order to craft yourself a suit of yak-hide armour.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Once you have a few pieces of yak-hide, return to me and I shall cure them for you.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Then I will give you instruction on how this hide may be crafted into a thick jerkin, ideal for protecting yourself from the granite clubs that the trolls of these isles prefer to wield.

steps.player: Thank you, Fridleif. I shall return with the yak-hides soon.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.player: I have still to complete the traditional armour of a Fremennik warrior.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: Thakkrad? Explain to [Fremennik name] what she needs to do again.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: You will need to cull several yaks in order to craft yourself a suit of yak-hide armour. There is a fenced-in field to the west of the village where yaks roam freely. Once you have a few pieces of yak-hide, return to me

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: To make the traditional armour of a Neitiznot warrior you will need some yak-hide to make the armour.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: Once you have the yak-hide, Thakkrad can cure it for you.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: To make the shield you will need some arctic pine, rope and bronze nails. Then you will need to find the 'Woodcutting stumps' to make make the shield on.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.player: Thanks for the advice, Fridlief. Where are these 'Woodcutting stumps'?

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: You will find the Woodcutting stumps near the town's 'geyser'.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.speaker: King Sorvott IV
gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.text: Oh, it's you. Why are you talking to me? Surely you should be hanging out with your Neitiznot friends now.

gear-of-a-champion-learning-about-the-ge.player: Alright I will - if that's the way you're going to be about it.

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: The aroma, outlander! It's very distinctive. So, do you wish to get your hide cured?

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: Have you completed your suit of yak armour?

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.player: Thakkrad has helped me to complete the traditional armour of a Fremennik warrior.

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: Excellent news. Now you have just one more item to craft and I can appoint you as leader of my warband; then you may lead our raid against the trolls.

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: The final piece of traditional arms is a large Fremennik round shield.

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: With this you will be able to deflect the large rocks that some of the trolls like to throw at you.

gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
gear-of-a-champion-making-yak-hide-armor.text: When you have all of these you should find the tree stump outside of my hut. You will be able to hammer together the shield.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: There is little more for me to say. You have proven your worth to my kinsmen and I, but I must continue with the traditions so...

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: 'I, [Fremennik name], swear to uphold the virtues of courage and honour.'

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.player: I [Fremennik name] swear to uphold the virtues of courage and honour.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: I hearby appoint [Fremennik name] as Champion of Neitiznot.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: Praise be; may the blood of our ancestors flow strongly in our new Champion.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: Welcome to the clan of Neitiznot; you shall be welcome in this township forever more.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: You have made our township very proud today. We hope you continue to match up to our hopes in the quest which we have for you.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: As my kinsmen have mentioned, there is a foul beast dwelling in the caves on the northernmost isle.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: We ask that you lead our militia against this brute and return with the beast's head as proof of your heroism.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: My guards have secured a foothold within the easternmost caves.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: We have not seen Jatizso's militia yet, but some of my scouts have reported hearing distant fighting in the tunnels.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.player: I shall make my way over to them now, so that we may defeat this foul Troll King.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: You should head to the eastern end of the northern isle. You don't want to run in to Jatizso's troops now.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: Fridleif's scouts have reported that the militia have entered the caves to the east of the northern isle. They are waiting for you to lead them in battle.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.player: Thanks Thakkrad, i'm on my way there now.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: Our militia have entered the caves to the east of the northern isle.

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.text: You should hurry to meet them before they are discovered by the trolls. Make sure you go to the right cave entrance, otherwise you won't find them!

gear-of-a-champion-swearing-your-oaths-t.player: Right, the eastern caves on the northern isle. Thanks Fridleif, I'm on my way there now.

facing-the-trolls-attempting-to-enter-th.text: Just inside the cave mouth lays the body of one of Jatizso's guards.
Maybe I should enter the caves to the east, so I can find Neitiznot's militia.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.player: Hmm. Left, right, then left again... I'm lost. Best I head toward the sound of the fighting.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Honour guard
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: The Champion had better arrive soon. We can't wait much longer!

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: [He/She] will be here soon. The Burgher trusts [Him/Her]. That's good enough for me.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: Sir, Champion [Fremennik name] has arrived! I knew [He/She] wouldn't let us down!

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.player: It was a hard journey here. I trust you all made it here intact?

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: A little bruised but nothing a true Fremennik can't handle!

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Honour guard
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: Our supplies are starting to run a little low; we should make our charge soon.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Honour guard
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: Once you have helped to slay 10 trolls then you should be able to assault the Troll King.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Honour guard
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: We will hold back the troll forces while you cross the bridge to the south of the cave.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.player: I will find the Troll King there, correct?

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: Yes [sir/madam]! I have some supplies with me if you need them, but I only have a small amount left. We took a heavy toll getting here.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.player: The fact you've saved any at all proves your bravery.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: Thank you [sir/madam]. We have food, Strength potions and Prayer potions to see us through this battle.

facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-entering-the-eastern-c.text: A fine tale we will tell once you have claimed the beast's head.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-bork.player: Bork! The battle rages on and we are strong, but I need supplies!

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-bork.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-bork.text: What do you need, brave [Fremennik name], [sir/madam]?

options.text: Give me food, Bork!

steps.player: Give me food, Bork!
Give me food, Bork!

steps.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
steps.text: Here, take this tuna quickly, [sir/madam]!
Bork Sigmundson hands you some Tuna.

options.text: I need Strength potions!

steps.player: I need Strength potions.
I need Strength potions.

steps.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
steps.text: Strength be with you, [Fremennik name]!
Bork Sigmundson hands you some Strength potions.

options.text: I need Prayer potions!

steps.player: I need Prayer potions.
I need Prayer potions.

steps.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
steps.text: May the gods be with you [Fremennik name]!
Bork Sigmundson hands you some Prayer potions.

options.text: I don't need anything.

steps.player: I don't need anything.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-bork-after-.speaker: Bork Sigmundson
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-bork-after-.text: I've run out of supplies, [Fremennik name]! Only our bravery remains.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.speaker: King Sorvott IV
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.text: My guards will beat you to your goal yet.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.speaker: King Sorvott IV
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.text: The weakness of wood and leather will be bested by my steel and mithril; mark my words.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.player: I sense defeat in your voice already, mighty King.
You and I both know that Burgher Burowgar's forces are better prepared and trained than your men.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.speaker: King Sorvott IV
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.text: Guards, prepare my gallows at once.

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.text: I would be leaving now if I were you, [Fremennik name].

facing-the-trolls-talking-to-king-sorvot.player: I think you're right Thorkel, goodbye.

facing-the-trolls-trying-to-cross-the-br.text: You have X more trolls to kill before you can kill the Troll King.
You have one more troll to kill before you can kill the Troll King.

facing-the-trolls-after-defeating-10-tro.text: You have defeated enough trolls to attack the King.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: King Sorvott IV
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: What are you doing in my court? Guards!

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.player: I have come to inform you that you may recall your guards; the Troll King was slain by my hand.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: King Sorvott IV
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Preposterous. Lies, I tell you, lies!

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Yes, your majesty, of course your majesty.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.player: Oh. Are they still recovering from their defeat against the trolls?

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: King Sorvott IV
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Outlander, leave me in peace before I am forced to bear arms against you myself.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.player: Very well, your Highness, I leave you to contemplate this...
Should you have approached me honestly and truthfully, rather than with lies and secrecy,
then it could have been you holding the head of the Troll King aloft today.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: King Sorvott IV
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Be gone with you. I have heard enough of your insults for one day.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Thanks, [Fremennik name], you are the first person to stand up to the King's bullying in many a year. Maybe he has learnt something today?

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Fare thee well brave warrior, fare thee well.

returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.speaker: Hrafn
returning-victorious-talking-to-king-sor.text: Purrrrz! (One wishes the tuna-bearing outlander well. One would prefer for [him/her] to stay.)

returning-victorious-talking-to-mord-gun.player: Heh. Thanks - I was pretty heroic even if I say so myself.

returning-victorious-talking-to-mord-gun.speaker: Mord Gunnars
returning-victorious-talking-to-mord-gun.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

returning-victorious-talking-to-thakkrad.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson/Fridleif Shieldson
returning-victorious-talking-to-thakkrad.text: Congratulations on defeating the Troll King. I hope you have collected the fine rewards that the Burgher Mawnis Burowgar has for you.

returning-victorious-returning-to-mawnis.player: I have returned victorious, Mawnis Burowgar.

returning-victorious-returning-to-mawnis.text: Without the ice troll king head:

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Do you bring proof of your victory?

steps.player: Nope.

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: You should bring proof to present to the Burgher.

returning-victorious-returning-to-mawnis.text: With the ice troll king head:

steps.player: I have returned victorious, Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Hail, Champion of Neitiznot.

steps.player: I offer the beast's head as proof that I have completed your task, sir.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: I thank you for bringing me this trophy, [Fremennik name], you have done much to bring honour to this isle.
You hold aloft the Troll King's head.

steps.player: My thanks for the honour you have bestowed upon me, Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.text: You hand the Troll King's head to Mawnis Burowgar.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: As a mark of my gratitude for slaying my nemesis, the foul Troll King, I offer you my helm.
The Burgher hands you his crown.

steps.player: I thank you for presenting me with such a finely crafted helm, sir.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: It makes me proud to know that the helm of my ancestors will be worn in battle.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: I thank you on behalf of all my Kinsmen, [Fremennik name].

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Praise be to our brave Champion.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: Hail, Champion [Fremennik name].

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Thakkrad, I believe you have finished repairing the remaining bridge.

steps.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
steps.text: That I have sir, we should be able to mine 'runite' once again; now that I have repaired the north-eastern bridge.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, so that is how we compete with the mineral wealth of Jatizso.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Indeed, the wealth of these isles may not be spread evenly, but we certainly make the most of what we have.

steps.player: I look forward to any other tasks you may have for me in the future, Burgher Burowar.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: My next task is to make peace with the King of Jatizso.

steps.player: I do not think I can help you with that sire. I don't think King Sorvott is speaking with me anymore.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Ah, I see you too have angered King Sorvott IV.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Not to worry, I have my ways of pacifying the King.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Fare thee well, my Champion.

steps.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
steps.text: Fare thee well.

steps.player: Fair thee well, kinsmen of Neitiznot.

steps.text: Congratulations! Quest complete!

post-quest-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
post-quest-talking-to-mawnis-burowgar.text: I am proud that the helm of my ancestors will be worn in battle. I thank you on behalf of all my kinsmen, [Fremennik name].

options.text: I thank you again for presenting me with such a helm.

steps.player: I thank you again for presenting me with such a helm.

options.text: Have you got any more of those helms?

steps.player: Have you got any more of those helms?

steps.text: If the player does not have any helms of Neitiznot in their inventory or bank:

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: What, the priceless heirloom that I gave to you as a sign of my trust and gratitude?

steps.player: Err yes, that one. I may have mislaid it.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: It's a good job I have alert and loyal men who notice when such a precious item is left laying around, and who pick it up.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: I'm afraid I'm going to have to charge you a 50,000 coin handling cost.
If the player does have a helm of Neitiznot in their inventory or bank:

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well, yes, I do. But I'm going to have to charge you 50,000 coins - these are precious, you know!
If the player doesn't have 50,000 coins in their inventory:

steps.player: I don't have that much money on me.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well, come back when you do.

options.text: Very well, I accept.

steps.player: Very well, I accept.

steps.text: Reclaim interface opens
If buying 1 helm:
The Burgher hands you his helm.
If buying more than 1 helm:
The Burgher hands you [number] helms.

options.text: I don't think I can afford that, sorry.

steps.player: I don't think I can afford that, sorry.

steps.speaker: Mawnis Burowgar
steps.text: Well, come back when you can.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: King Sorvott IV
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: What are you doing in my court? Guards!

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.player: I have come to inform you that you may recall your guards; the Troll King was slain by my hand.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: King Sorvott IV
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: Preposterous. Lies, I tell you, lies!

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: Yes, your majesty, of course your majesty.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.player: Oh. Are they still recovering from their defeat against the trolls?

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: King Sorvott IV
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: Outlander, leave me in peace before I am forced to bear arms against you myself.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.player: Very well, your Highness, I leave you to contemplate this...
Should you have approached me honestly and truthfully, rather than with lies and secrecy,
then it could have been you holding the head of the Troll King aloft today.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: King Sorvott IV
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: Be gone with you. I have heard enough of your insults for one day.

post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.speaker: Thorkel Silkbeard
post-quest-talking-to-king-sorvott.text: Thanks, [Fremennik name], you are the first person to stand up to the King's bullying in many a year. Maybe he has learnt something today?

post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.speaker: Trogen Konungarde/Kjedelig Uppsen
post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.text: Ho, [Fremennik name]! The brave warrior returns!

post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.player: It was a hard-fought battle, but we Fremennik prevailed!

post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.speaker: Trogen Konungarde/Kjedelig Uppsen
post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.text: I expect we'll be hearing songs about the 'Slayer of the Troll King' for many years to come.

post-quest-talking-to-trogen-or-kjedelig.player: It would be an honour to be remembered in such a way! Thanks.

post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.text: Thank you for leading the Burgher's militia against the Troll King.

post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.text: Now that the trolls are leaderless I have repaired the bridge to the central isle for you as best I can.

post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.player: Thanks Thakkrad. Does that mean I have access to the runite ores on that island?

post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
post-quest-talking-to-thakkrad.text: Yes, you should be able to mine runite there if you wish.

post-quest-talking-to-fridleif.speaker: Fridleif Shieldson
post-quest-talking-to-fridleif.text: Congratulations, Champion [Fremennik name]. Thank you for defeating the Troll King.

9k9fzt.speaker: Maria Gunnars
9k9fzt.text: You should speak with my husband.

PxCPs9.player: I just stopped to say hello.

PxCPs9.speaker: Maria Gunnars
PxCPs9.text: Thanks, and good luck with the Burgher's tasks.

_sfvGe.speaker: Thakkrad Sigmundson
_sfvGe.text: You don't have space for the Burgher's reward.

75917o.player: I'll think about it a bit.

iv8KYz.speaker: [Merchant]
iv8KYz.text: You do not need to collect taxes from me this time. Begone with you!
